utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Could I remind you of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence which still applies. Mr. Domazet, had you concluded?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. Not yet. I do have some questions left. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Good morning to you, sir. If you remember, we broke for the day yesterday when we talked about you arriving in the hospital on the 15th of November. You say that you went with your wife straight to that corridor on the ground floor, or the mezzanine, depending on your perspective, but there were no patients there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In view of these several days that you spent at the hospital and also taking into account your testimony yesterday, you were able to see a number of well-known people who were there, either as patients or those who simply came to the hospital at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to see if there was any security there, anyone providing security for the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any security officers anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: During your stay there, you realised that there was some detained JNA soldiers there being treated at the hospital, JNA soldiers who had been taken prison.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, I heard of one. I think this person was a JNA officer. I heard of one such case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember the name, by any chance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you see this person? Do you know which part of the hospital he was in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see him. My understanding at the time was there was a JNA officer, a single JNA officer, in the hospital somewhere at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you see Marin Vidic, Bili, at the hospital at any time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know what he was doing there? Did you speak to him or did you just --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just saw him in passing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you specify the time, please, in relation to your time at the hospital between the 15th and the 19th.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact day, but I must have seen him two or three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I'm sure you remember yesterday, in answer to one of the questions asked by my learned friend, you identified quite a number of people from that list that you were shown, people you had seen at the hospital. Now, it appears that you knew some of these people in one way or another. Can you tell me what they did in Vukovar exactly. What were they doing before the war and what were they doing at the hospital? What about Ivo Ismet Ahmetovic, what do you know about this person and when did you see him at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him when I arrived at the hospital. I must have seen him about two or three times. There were many wounded there and many people in general. We didn't meet too many times; it must have been two or three occasions, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What did he do for a living?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was no hospital employee, if that's what you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know if he was one of Vukovar's defenders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you saw him at the hospital, was he in uniform, was he in civilian clothes, some sort of an overcoat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I saw him, he was in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Tomislav Bajnrauch, or Ivan Bajnrauch - I suppose they're related - what can you tell me about these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tomislav Bajnrauch was with me in the civil protection detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know when he arrived at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was coming to the hospital a lot due to the nature of his job.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So what job was it that he had with the civil protection detail and that had to do with the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in charge of the food and water supplies, primarily for patients but also for the hospital's medical staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I suppose you know this because he was there with you throughout. He had not been wounded and was not at the hospital as a patient, was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's right, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What about Ivan Bajnrauch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if they're related or not because I just know these people by sight. I don't know them well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: But you saw Ivan Bajnrauch at the hospital too, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What about him; was he a defender, too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What sort of clothes was he wearing when you saw him? Was he wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if he was wounded or not, but he was wearing civilian clothes; that much I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What about Lovro Barbir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lovro Barbir was an elderly man. He was a neighbour of mine in the centre of town. He was at the hospital because his wife was a hospital employee.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What about Ante Bodrozic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a waiter in the Danube Hotel. He was not a hospital employee.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was he a defender, too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Josip Bradaric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We worked together at my company. He was a commercial salesman or something like that and he was with me at the hospital; I saw him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was he involved in the town's defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about him. I don't know that he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did he work as a police officer at any time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What about Zvonimir Caleba?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Caleta.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Caleta.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Another waiter from the Danube Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Up until the war, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What about during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea. I saw him at the hospital; that was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Stanko Duvnjak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a police officer of the Vukovar MUP. He was at the hospital because he had been wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Vinko Ebner, Djuro?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know this person by sight. He hails from Sarengrad and I suppose that's where he lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What was he doing at the hospital, do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea, but I don't think he was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was he a defender, too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What about Milan Grejza?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was an active-duty police officer with the Ministry of Internal Affairs Vukovar detachment. He had been wounded in his leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Sinisa Glavasevic, he was a journalist; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew all about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When did you see him at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see him at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I think you described him yesterday as another person you had seen at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible, but right now it escapes me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What about Tomislav Hegedus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Another active-duty police officer with the Vukovar MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Throughout the war; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You saw him at the hospital, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When and how, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was just in passing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You say "in passing." Was he passing or were you passing? Did you bump into each other somewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were passing one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So he wasn't in a prone position because he was wounded, lying somewhere in a bed in a hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't really notice that. I didn't notice if he was wounded not, if that's what you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Nikica Holjevac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him sitting on one of those auxiliary beds, but not much apart from that. I think he was a local journalist.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Boris Antol?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Boris Jantol.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You identified him yesterday as another person you saw at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: His wife and their two-month baby was with me in that shelter across the way from the hospital. He came often, needless to say, to see his wife. I used to see him quite often around Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was he a defender, too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember when exactly you saw him at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What about Branko Lukenda?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Likewise, an active-duty police officer in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You saw him in the hospital; do you remember when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can no longer remember exactly when I saw all these people individual -- individually.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What about Milan Magdic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a waiter in the Lav Hotel. He was seriously wounded and he was lying in a bed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What about Sinisa Veber? Did you see this person at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sinisa Veber was also at the hospital, but not wounded. He was also one of the town's defenders.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Mate Vlaho?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A hospital employee.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What about Ivan Vulic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two persons called Ivan Vulic. Which one do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You talked about one of them yesterday as another person you saw at the hospital. In case you saw both, please provide information in relation to both of them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The younger one was the one that I was talking about. He had a Band-Aid over one of his eyes, or on one of his eyes. I saw him out in the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Wearing what sort of clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was he a defender, too, do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What about Zvonko Vulic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wounded, too. He had a leg wound. I saw him lying in a bed, but I don't know if he was a defender or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I think you said that he was sitting on a bed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Because what I see in the transcript does not reflect your words. What about all these people we have been mentioning; did any of them join you on the way to Velepromet? Could you see what was happening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember any of those people on my -- on my truck or arriving at Velepromet and Vupik.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When the transport was on its way, the one you've described, can you tell us if all the civilians from the hospital were on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know about the one that I was on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know about the fact that some people stayed behind at the hospital, although they were civilians and, according to what had been said, they were supposed to go to Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did hear that some civilians remained.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Speaking about the transport, you said there -- you said there were over ten military trucks involved, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did those military trucks have a tarpaulin? Were they covered and did they have the ladders to climb in order to get on the truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So you would get up the ladder and board the truck; that's how you got on, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In answer to one of the questions you were asked, you talked about a number of persons mentioned in the Vukovar official note. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Just a couple of words about this official note for the benefit of the Trial Chamber. I believe you know about this because you worked at the hospital. An official note is a record of something that a MUP official took as a statement, but it's not really an accurate record and is never signed as a rule. Would that seem to be a fair summary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You gave a statement to a MUP officer on the 15th of May, 1992. That's what the note reflects, but the note was compiled five days later, on the 20th of May. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is indeed what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you agree with me, sir, that before this trial began this statement was never shown to you by any police officers and such-like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you spoke about the persons in that official note, you said that all of them were armed and wearing all kinds of uniforms, as you said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You also said at one point that you believed all of them to be members of Serb paramilitary formations, but you were not able to tell which ones exactly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I still believe that. Back then, however, I had no idea who belonged to which unit or who had what sort of insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you speak about Serb paramilitary units, do you also include the Territorial Defence of the Serbian Krajina which was set up at one time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Were members of the Krajina TO wearing the olive-drab uniforms that were used by the JNA, too?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the witness's answer; could the witness please be asked to repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get your answer, sir, to my last question. Can you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said they were wearing all different kinds of uniform. Because I simply didn't know at the time who belonged to which unit, I wasn't able to distinguish.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Were you able to distinguish these people from those who were usually described as the Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was able and I am able to distinguish them from those.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: By what means? Uniform? Insignia? Something else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the insignia, I believe. I believe that to be the only distinction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you looked at that list yesterday and you spoke about each of the individual names on that list, you said you believed them all to be members of Serb paramilitary units. Does that mean that in your opinion none of the persons you identified was a regular JNA soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think any of them were, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You identified one of those people as Zigic with the rank of major. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said he was wearing some sort of a dark brown uniform, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What kind of uniform was it exactly? Was it the olive-drab uniform or was that a different uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zigic used to work with me in the Vukovar MUP. He was a senior inspector, police inspector. When I saw him, he had one of those officer's uniforms on; it was brown and it was the JNA type.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: But what kind exactly; the olive-drab one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the ceremonial one, the brown uniform worn by high-ranking officers. I'm not sure how I should put that to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You are a reserve officer yourself. Was that a reserve officer's uniform or --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was brown -- a brown uniform is a brown uniform. It was dark brown, moreover.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Both parts of the uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: From what you told us, one could see that he was from Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he had been born in Vukovar, but he spent many years as an inspector with the MUP and he was my senior.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Stanko Vujanovic, do you know that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stanko Vujanovic, the taxi driver?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Is he Zigic's brother-in-law?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Son-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: To a question posed yesterday as to what room at Velepromet you were taken to, you said the room that was later called the room of death. You said that some called it a carpenter shop and other ones called it the room of death. When was it that you heard about this room of death for the first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upon our return from the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you talked about boarding the buses, having left the room where you were, and I believe your bus was right behind the military Pinzgauer, there were no follow-up questions about that topic but I wanted to ask you now whether you were mistreated, either yourself or any of the other people on the bus subsequently.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I meant during the time the bus was there before it started moving and until you reached Sremska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to Sremska Mitrovica, there was no abuse.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Since you used to work with the police, although you had left prior to the events concerned, did you used to know Ivan Micanin? He used to be employed with the Vukovar MUP.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the name?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Ivo Micanin.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Franjo Kracak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do; he used to be a carpenter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know what he used to do during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my stay in the hospital, or before that, I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you hear that he was later accused of crimes committed against Serbian population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You probably know who Tomislav Mercep was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Franjo Kracak, was he a member of his group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't associate with those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you were asked about planes yesterday, you mentioned the two and you heard that they were shot down but that you did not see that yourself. That was at the beginning of the conflict in Vukovar; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you at any later stage hear that any other planes were shot down in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were different rumours. I didn't see any of that myself, and one has to make a distinction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know where the main headquarters were in Vukovar during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if there ever was such a thing as main headquarters. As I said, Vukovar was trying to defend itself in its entirety, and each individual part of the city probably had its own command or, as you call it, HQ. As for the main HQ, I wouldn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: But you probably know who was the chief commander in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At what time?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: During the conflict.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe there were two.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, and where did their HQ -- where was it located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I didn't use to go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In your statement given to the OTP, by the end you cited a conclusion of yours and I wanted to ask you if you are still of that opinion. You said: "My conclusion was that they -- the JNA did not know that the other Serbs were to commit crimes against us." You said that then; do you still abide by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I stated in the statement and I still believe it was so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I have no further questions. I thank you for your answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this concludes my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Domazet. Ms. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone present in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir. My name is Mira Tapuskovic. I am one of the counsel for Mr. Miroslav Radic. During the years you spent working in your profession, so as not to go into detail and not to reveal your identity, but at the time did you have an opportunity to go to the building of Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At what time?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Before the outbreak of the conflict in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was able to, but I never went there.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So you never actually went to the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you explained the sequence of events at Velepromet, and we used a chart made by yourself.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received that chart.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You said somebody made that for you some six months ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was it a friend of yours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was that a copy of a cadastre plan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems so.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: As for the numbers on the sketch, do they tell you anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The handwritten remarks or markings on individual facilities, were those made by yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When your friend made that sketch for you, did you give him any instructions as to how to go about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Does the sketch reflect the current situation at Velepromet or, rather, does it reflect the situation as it was 14 years ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as he told me and as far as he is concerned, this is the current situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. To go back to the period when you were inside the shelter, do you know what the large shelters in Vukovar were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Were those Olajnica 1 and Olajnica 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and Komerc Borovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did that also include the buildings of Alpina and Varteks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: As well as the schools of Vladimir Nazor and a large shelter at Strossmayer Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know about both of them or either of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know for both of the shelters.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Were you given a weapon when you overtook your duties with the civilian protection and when you started distributing food and medication?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never used to have a weapon. I wasn't given one.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: We heard a witness from the civilian protection who was a colleague of yours who said he did have a weapon. What about other members of the civil protection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. As for the people who were with me, they didn't, and there were members of the civilian protection around -- across the city.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When you testified before the Belgrade court, you said that you were assigned to the civilian protection. Could you tell us by whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I was a handicapped person, I went there myself to see what it was that I could do, and then they sent me to civilian protection.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear you properly. What did you do exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to their staff and I told them that I wanted to do something. They told me to stay there, with their organisation, and that I could help there.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you then what shelters you were to service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I -- what shelters in particular?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just one. There was a large apartment block across from the hospital, next to the cemetery. It had a large shelter in the basement.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that there was -- there were reserves of food for the hospital there as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was on the upper floor; it used to be a small department store.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What about the warehouse itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was some food there as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You said that in that warehouse, as you replied yesterday to an OTP question, that in that warehouse -- pardon me, shelter, not a warehouse, but rather a shelter, that there were between 50 to 60 people there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And you said those were mostly elderly people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and a few women with small children.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where younger men from that area were, from the area serviced by that shelter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I already mentioned, next to the building where I was there was a large military apartment block. Those were military retirees, elderly people with their spouses. They all came to that shelter, and they were with us until the end.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. But I asked you about younger men.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the younger men. They were probably somewhere outside.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday and in your statement you said that the soldiers and the military and the policemen used to come to the shelter and used to inform you about the situation in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: As a member of the civilian protection who worked in medication distribution as well as food distribution, did you used to leave the shelter and see what the situation was in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it was in the environs of the hospital and the apartment block where the shelter was.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Since your duty was to distribute food and medication, how come you only went as far as the hospital? Does that mean that your particular warehouse supplied the hospital exclusively with food and medication?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes; the hospital plus the people in the shelter.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You also said that the police station was damaged by shelling. That building is in close proximity to the hospital, making it very close to the shelter where you were.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I wasn't quite focussed, but could you tell me, when was the police station hit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some ten days before that. I arrived around the 15th of October, and it may have been damaged some ten days prior to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That is quite precise. You said that the policemen from the station came to the shelter as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that the commander of the Vukovar police station, Stipe Pole, came there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Stipe Pole, is that his full name or his first name Stjepan Pole?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes; Stjepan Pole.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Those policemen, including Stjepan Pole, they were there until your departure to the hospital on the 15th of October [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they stayed even longer after I left.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement you mention that 90 per cent of the people from the shelter that you were in accompanied you to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If 90 per cent of the people went, then it means that also some MUP members who were in the shelter went to the hospital as well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I said a minute ago, they remained behind.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: How many MUP members did come to the shelter in the first place, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is difficult to say. I can't even approximate.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Were all those people that you mentioned today and when answering to my colleague Mr. Domazet's questions, as members of the MUP and for whom you said you saw in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: How can you say then that they remained behind when you told Mr. Domazet that you saw them in the hospital? It means that most of the policemen, perhaps not on the same day, but most of them did leave the shelter and go to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, for the transcript there's an error and I suspect my learned friend would want it to be right. At 20.11, it refers to October, not November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can't see the transcript from where I'm standing, so I would like to thank my colleague.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You were telling us about how the people who organised Vukovar's defence tried to breakthrough. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Inter alia, did you hear as to when they tried to break out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I heard, they tried on several occasions, depending on when somebody wanted to do something.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Since you confirmed that you witnessed a conversation between Marin Vidic, Bili, and Dr. Bosanac together -- and their conversation with the commander of the police station, did you overhear then about who was to join the attempt to break out and who was to stay in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't close enough to hear who was to stay and who was to go.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But you said that you were close enough to overhear their conversation about signing an agreement, or truce, as well as about evacuation. So what did you hear exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever meet Mile Dedakovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never, until the present day.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know until what time was he a commander of Vukovar's defence? A minute ago you said that there were two people at the head of the staff.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he left at some point but he never returned.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know when exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't. I don't want to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where he went to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on I heard that he had left to Vinkovci.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And then he headed the Zupanja-Vukovar operations group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that the first attempts of breaking out were as early as early November?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which attempts do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The one you mentioned in your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when people tried to break out.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The civilian protection, was it organised in a way that other members, apart from yourself because you said that you mainly serviced the hospital, but did other members move in between various shelters and warehouses and were they distributed in various places?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that your colleagues from the civilian protection had any problems with the minefields?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Since you were distributing food and medication, what did you know about the food warehouse at Nama?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the shelling of Vukovar began, the Nama department store was completely burnt to the ground on two occasions and I don't know whether there was any such thing as a food warehouse there.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What do you know about the forces in Bogdanovci, Croatian defence forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't go there.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But you said that both policemen and soldiers came to your shelter and that they used to report on the situation in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I interrupted you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They came there individually, but nobody reported in the strict sense of -- in the strict meaning of the word. Nobody told me about the numbers of people defending Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The HOS forces were at Negoslavci?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see them there.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear about whether they were there or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who Blago Zadro was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who Robert Zadro was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a son of his.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Blago Zadro was killed on the 16th of October.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Borovo Naselje.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: At Trpinjska Cesta.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in its close proximity.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see Stjepan Pole after that in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Since you said there were 50 to 60 civilians, that is elderly people, as you put it, in the shelter and that the soldiers and the policemen from the military -- from the police station came, what was the total number of the people in the shelter at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only repeat yet again that I did not pay much attention to the number of the policemen.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps we could use the same method then used by our esteemed colleague to guess. Could you tell us if there were more than 10 or more than 20?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe there were more than 20, if I have to mention a certain figure.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You said that in the shelter when the head of hospital, Dr. Bosanac, came, that there were means of radio communication there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A police telephone was installed there. I'm not an expert, I don't know its proper name.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But you say that this was a police phone; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was this something that was brought over from the police station itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You say there was communication and you say that you could hear conversations. What did you overhear of the conversation between Vesna Bosanac and whoever happened to be at the other end?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I couldn't exactly hear everything that was being said, but I heard that negotiations were underway for an evacuation to take place, that the buses would soon be there, and that the negotiations were going quite well.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if there was more radio equipment elsewhere in Vukovar, in a different shelter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let us now briefly go to what was going on at the hospital. You said in your statement to the OTP that the Chetniks arrived at the hospital together with JNA soldiers. Further, you testified in the Dokmanovic case on page 551, line 2, that the Chetniks were outside the building, in the courtyard. Sir, can you remember precisely where the Chetniks were at the time -- or rather, those units which you at the time described as Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This has to be a mistake. I said -- or rather, I assumed that when the JNA arrived at the hospital they were followed by paramilitaries. When I came out on the hospital steps, they were in the group, moving about the hospital courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When you testified in the Belgrade trial by videolink, you confirmed that the hospital was first reached by people from Vukovar and from elsewhere, and it was only after this that the JNA eventually arrived.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that would have been feasible. I don't think that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't want to interrupt my learned friend, but perhaps it's necessary at this stage. She has made a reference to the Dokmanovic trial, 551, line 2, in relation to Chetniks. I don't have that particular reference. I haven't got any reference to Chetnik at all. If it is there - and I repeat, which I've said before - perhaps it might be prudent for the document to be put before the witness so that we're absolutely correct. And it also applies to any other challenges going to be put.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It seems that Mr. Moore can't find any reference to Chetniks at that page, Ms. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the word "Chetnik" is not to be found on that page; I agree with my learned friend Mr. Moore. I am, as we speak, looking at that page. I just wanted to use a shortcut, as it were, because at one time in his testimony the witness refers to these people as "natives of Vukovar" and "local Serb forces," and on a different occasion he refers to them as "the Chetniks." I referred to the previous page of the transcript, but I just wanted to cut across, as it were, just for us to be able to ascertain what those groups were, regardless of what the witness called them at various times, and when these groups reached the hospital in relation to when the JNA people got there. But I believe we can obtain clarification from the witness himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I agree with that. The problem is that the transcript then suggests that the witness has changed his account in a material way because he no longer says there were Chetniks, whereas, as you have just indicated, you're merely searching to get from him who he says was there, so that to misquote the transcript of a previous trial can leave the record with quite a misleading indication of the witness's position. So if you could be much more careful about that, please, and if you are going to be trying to pin a witness down to something that he said before, or she has said, it would be important to let the witness see the previous transcript or statement or whatever it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I fully accept your criticism; that much is certain. I will try to avoid this sort of practice in future. I cannot confront this witness with the transcript because the transcript is in English. It may have been my mistake not reading back the relevant part to the witness, but please accept my apologies. I will now move on and try to avoid such mistakes in future.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let us now move on to what happened at Vupik. You said that you were separated from the group by Darko Fot, you and a number of other persons. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, did you know any of those people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did Darko Fot make any threats to you at the time? Was it at gunpoint that he took you across to the Velepromet building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Why did you then cross with Darko Fot, alongside with a number of other people, from Vupik to Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was me, Aleksandar Cotar, and a number of other people -- a number of other people were added to that group, and then Darko told us: Now we're walking across the road to Velepromet, and that was all.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you reached Velepromet, did you see any JNA people there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean across the way, at Velepromet? I didn't notice any there.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You gave us a detailed account yesterday, using the sketch that you brought, of how Boro Zuvanovic approached you, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was another man before he came.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But that's not the one I'm asking about. I'm asking you about Boro Zuvanovic, aren't I?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You said he took you and another man called Jurica down a route which you marked as the route stretching from B to C on that map. Do you still remember that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So this time when you went with Jurica and Boro Zuvanovic, were only the three of you there or was there anyone else around at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the three of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you walk side by side or in a line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Boro was walking between the two of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: It was entirely dark by this time; night had fallen at Velepromet.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You said there were quite many people there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If we look at the sketch we get an idea of the distance involved, but could you please try to specify in metres the distance between the place where you were standing before you were approached by Boro Zuvanovic and the spot that Boro Zuvanovic took you to with Jurica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really say, not even a ballpark figure, but it's quite a long way.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us if en route from B to C there were other persons passing you, people who were at Velepromet at the same time as you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several people passed us on the way. This was not very close to where most of the things were happening outside the administration building.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that the Chetniks - I'm talking about your statement in B/C/S, page 5, second passage --

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, Your Honours, I'm trying very hard not to make any erroneous indication.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You say that the Chetniks were using electric torches.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was across the way; that was at Vupik.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Were they using any sort of torches around here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You passed a person called Capalo on the way there, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In the official note dated the 15th of May, 1992, and in your statement, you mentioned that Capalo was carrying something in his hand.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a knife.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: There you go. You also said that he was carrying something else in his other hand, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a human head. I would say I'm about 99 per cent certain about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You said yesterday you were 99 per cent certain about this being a human head.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In that official note you specified it was the head of an unknown young man. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: That may be because you never actually saw this official note until you arrived here to testify.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's what I've said, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When you testified in the Dokmanovic case, you didn't mention this scene at all, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody asked.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When you testified in Belgrade, you never referred to this particular occurrence, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody asked.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In preparation for this testimony as you were being proofed by the OTP, did anyone refresh your memory or show you the official note and your official statement from 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had those, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You saw Jankovic [as interpreted] before Boro Zuvanovic appeared, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if Jankovic [as interpreted] actually addressed you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What exactly did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In the Dokmanovic case, page 555, lines 1 through 5 on the transcript, you were asked specifically --

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may, I don't wish to extemporise and I need to go back to the transcript and quote the relevant passage for the witness. Your Honours, I'll have to first read the witness's answer where he refers to this person. [In English] "Again, I was taken out of this group by another man. His name was Mico Dzankovic. I knew him personally, too. He was a waiter in Vukovar." [Interpretation] My question: [In English] "Did he say anything to you? "A. No."

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, these are your words, words you uttered while testifying in the Dokmanovic case. In the Belgrade case, the Ovcara case, on page 7, lines 10 through 12, you say that he addressed you by name and asked you what you were doing there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But in the Dokmanovic case you said he never spoke to you. When answering my first question, you seem to have suggested that he told you something different. Yet now you confirm that he told you what I've just read back to you. He called you by your name and he asked you what you were doing there. You're under oath here, sir; I hope you understand that. Can you please describe what exactly transpired between you and Mico Dzankovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. I have no more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this completes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Given the time, we might have the break now, do you think, Mr. Bulatovic? There are redactions, so it will need to be half an hour. We will resume at 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's really in relation to Ms. Tapuskovic's cross-examination vis-a-vis what was said in the Belgrade trials for this witness, clearly the point being, as the Defence would see it, the apparent inconsistency. I mean no discourtesy at all to my learned friend; I know how difficult it is sometimes to cross-examine, but I would submit that there may be an element of inaccuracy in the account put to the witness. And perhaps the safest way would be for the witness to be reminded exactly of what was said and then it's on the record and the Court can draw its own conclusions if there be inconsistency or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Moore. Yes, Mr. Bulatovic. If you would be good enough, if you're cross-examining on what was said in the trial in Belgrade, to quote precisely the passage you're relying on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's obviously the way I put it: It's actually the questions that have been put by Ms. Tapuskovic that there may be the inconsistency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: No, it's -- so it's really -- the witness should have the opportunity of having rehearsed to him again what was actually said in Belgrade by Ms. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Why don't you do that in cross-examination, Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Very well, of course. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Bulatovic, I thought it was something you had done. So please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning to you, sir. I'm Momcilo Bulatovic, co-counsel for Mr. Sljivancanin. You have been asked quite a number of questions by both my learned friend from the OTP and my fellow Defence teams. I will do my best not to ask any redundant questions, any questions already answered, but whenever clarification is required I will make sure to raise any matters. Sir, please make a pause between my question and your answer because we happen to speak the same language, more or less the same language, that is. In your statement to the OTP, there is one piece of information that is slightly different from what you told us here. I hope to keep your identity safe, but this has to do with your years of service. You said that you worked for a certain institution from 1974 until 1984, and here you said from 1971 until 1981.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the latter. I was working in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Your personal information indicates that you have the reserve rank of second lieutenant. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You say that you are a disabled person. When did your disability occur, so to speak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was between 1981 and 1982.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And when did you leave the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult to remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: But it was certainly before your disability. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: As second lieutenant, did you ever take part in any military drills? Were you called up at any time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean after my regular military service?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you sign for any military equipment as a second lieutenant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What about the ranks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not for the purpose of military drills.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And other than that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had no ranks at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The number of questions that I'm about to ask might endanger the protective measures for this witness, so I believe it might be a good idea to go briefly into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: As you went about your duties as specified a while ago, were you ever in touch with any of the people you mentioned, the people you saw at the hospital or at Velepromet, the people from Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember encountering any of them in any official capacity.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did any of these people you've mentioned here ever break the law and maybe it was that sort of situation where you encountered some of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You say "perhaps." Can you please tell the Court which of these people had form, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dzankovic was convicted for murder before the war. It was at the tip in Vukovar that he murdered somebody.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know -- did you know anything about the criminal past, as it were, of the man you refer to as Capalo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a petty gambler, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever come across Mr. Martin Dosen while you were working as a police officer? Do you know what he did in his own spare time, so to speak, because we know that he worked as a professional fisherman for a while, but before that he had a different job.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He worked at the Borovo factory and later became a professional fisherman. I didn't know that much about his private life, but I know that he liked to play cards.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if Martin Dosen was in touch with somebody named Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I've never heard anything about that. First I hear of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In order to go back to some of my opening questions, I want to discuss the shelter to which you went. If I understand you correctly, that was the Vupik shelter, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was in the Vupik building.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said how many people there were there. Let's go back to the point in time when the police came. This is something my learned friend Ms. Tapuskovic asked you about. Was there anything else in the Vupik factory where you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Vupik, just in case you know, does it have any other shelters, apart from this one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. This was a residential building belonging to Vupik; three floors, a shop on the ground floor, and down in the cellar there was a large shelter running the entire length of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Does the name Zvezdana Polovina ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think she worked as a journalist in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where Radio Vukovar was physically located? Later on it was renamed Croatian Radio Vukovar, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Early on they were across the way from the main pharmacy in Vukovar. It was at the junction near the Pecanski Kriz town centre near the Danube hotel. That's where the building was physically located and I suppose they had a shelter in that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if Croatian Radio Vukovar was ever moved to any of Vupik's shelters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke about the existence of police radio -- of a police radio link between the Vupik shelter and the outside world, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In that same shelter, did they have a phone link as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I'm talking about. That's the only thing there was; there was a phone link which the officers used to communicate. That's the extent of what I witnessed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Was that just an ordinary phone link or a special phone link? After all, you worked with this institution which I'll avoid mentioning now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't really focus on that. I didn't need to focus on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Was there a different kind of link in addition to this telephone link between the MUP members, who were in the same shelter as you, linking them to a third party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they had Motorolas; you know, those mobile radio stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you at any time use this radio equipment or the Motorolas from the shelter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you listen to any conversations that the MUP members staying in the shelter were having over the radio link or Motorola?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on several occasions, but I wasn't really paying close attention. I didn't even like to listen to their conversations. I no longer worked in the same profession as they and I was no longer as interested, not interested enough to listen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You answered a previous question by saying that you did not know the exact number of police officers who came to the Vupik shelter.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember the exact date in relation to your departure for the hospital? When did they come there in relation to your departure for the field hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About ten days earlier. I believe that's what I stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said that people from the hospital used to come to the shelter; Dr. Bosanac in particular. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Throughout the ten days -- or rather, maybe I should ask how often?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I said I saw her twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of Dr. Matos?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did he come to the shelter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement you said that soldiers and policemen came to the shelter to keep you informed. I'm interested, why did they come to you, or do you know whether those policemen and soldiers went to some other shelters to inform some other people as to what was going on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since some family members of certain defenders of Vukovar were there - for example, I mentioned the wife and the 2-month-old baby - people used to drop by, and of course we were interested in the events and what was going on outside. That's how we were kept informed, by what they could tell us as to what was going on in the outside world.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Among the people who -- from the MUP who came to the hospital -- to the shelter, was one of them Stipe Pole?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: The name of Ivo Arbanas, does it tell you anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what it was that you heard.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard he was a defender in the town of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. You mentioned that when Dr. Bosanac would come around to the shelter and through the -- your conversations with police members, that it was that way you learned that she was negotiating with the JNA.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: How often did you ever hear such conversations? Did you hear the contents, and do you know what was the topic of those negotiations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said she came twice - at least, I saw her twice - and they always discussed these negotiations. What I heard was that the negotiations were going rather well and that things would be fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from Dr. Bosanac, who else participated in the negotiations? As I presume that if she wanted to discuss anything with anyone, she could have chosen any particular location, hence she may have been joined by someone else in the shelter.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Marijan -- Marin Vidic, Bili, accompanied her.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know why it was that they came to your particular shelter and why did they negotiate from your shelter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think they were conducting any negotiations from there. They came to inform or, rather, coordinate with the police commander in Vukovar, who was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: That is what I was interested in. Since you made that conclusion that she wanted to speak with the commander of the police, do you know what it was they spoke about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything as to the contents of the evacuation agreement? Since you learned that the negotiations were going well, do you know what was inside or part of the agreement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That there were going to be around 50 buses and that people will be allowed to go where they went, depending on their own wish, and that the city would be handed over, and that there would be no problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you overhear that in one of the conversations or were you told that by anyone in the shelter; perhaps by Dr. Bosanac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I overheard their conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether there has been an agreement to complete the negotiations process? Has anything been signed anywhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never seen any such thing and I never heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: For how long have you known Dr. Bosanac, and how well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've known her for a few years now -- that is, I had known her for a few years before the war. She used to be a paediatrician and she treated my children.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And that was your only contact with her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: By the way, do you know anything of Dr. Bosanac's husband, what he was doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name was Lavoslav, and he was a construction engineer with the construction department of the Borovo company.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: During the events in question, do you know what his activities were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout my time in Vukovar, I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what happened with Dr. Bosanac's sons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: To go back to the shelter, in one part of your statement and in your testimony here you said that after you left to the hospital you also went to a few other shelters to tell people to go to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't me. We sent some other people to tell others to go to the hospital. It wasn't me personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So who decided to send those people over and with what task?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one made any decision. It was a spontaneous thing to do, to tell those people to come to the hospital to be in greater numbers. We thought that there was security in numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the events of the 18th of November, 1991, in Vukovar, specifically did you know that the so-called Croatian army at Mitnica surrendered on that day?
