utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that, together with those people, a large number of civilians from Mitnica surrendered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where those civilians used to be accommodated? Where were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since that part of the town at Mitnica is uneven and there were numerous cellars, private cellars, as well as rather large houses, I believe those people were in those cellars throughout.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: That was up to the 18th, but I was interested in where were they after they came out of those cellars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether those people were at Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said you came to the Vukovar Hospital on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And that you stayed there until the 19th.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said that the number of civilians was constantly increasing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where all of them came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I hope it was from the town of the -- of Vukovar and from the environs of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Are you certain about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the number of such civilians. If you agree, there were about 2500 people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my estimate, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Could that mean that there were more?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You would agree that it put a lot of pressure on the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when most of the civilians came to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 18th.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where those civilians were accommodated at the hospital, because 2500 is a large number.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The hospital is rather big, and there was the old building of the hospital. People used all available space where they felt safe or even where they did not feel so safe. They were everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood properly, there were some in the old hospital building as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were cellars there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In that period between the 15th and the 19th of November, 1991, when you were at the hospital, you were not in the same place throughout the four days, I presume.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, of course. I walked around the hospital where my wife was, together with my friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I presume your wife and your friends were in different parts of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we were together in the same group; that was the group from the shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you meet any of the hospital employees that you knew from before? For example, Dr. Njavro?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Then Dr. Bosanac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you discuss anything with them? Did any of the people near you speak to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had questions. Basically, the only question we had was how things would conclude, what would happen to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You were present during some conversations between Dr. Bosanac and another person in the shelter on the 15th. Then you saw her between the 15th and the 19th in the hospital. You asked her about what was to happen with all of you, and you must have discussed this with some other civilians as well. So what was your conclusion as to what was to happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never spoke with Dr. Bosanac alone. There were many people around. They all spoke with her. We all wanted to know and demanded to be told what the result of the talks were and what was to happen. The constant answer was, as I described, was that there were to be buses and that people are supposed to express their wish as to where to go to. That was the standard reply circulating the hospital, and it resounded in everyone's ears.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: On the 18th in the evening, since that was the day before your departure from the hospital, did you hear in any part of the hospital or from anybody that any sort of agreement had been signed concerning evacuation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In your discussions either with Dr. Bosanac or with Mr. Bilic or with any of the passers-by, people you spoke with, did you hear of an agreement being reached and that it should include only the wounded and the hospital employees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I was sufficiently clear before when I said that we heard that all the people are to leave Vukovar, depending on where they wanted to go. As concerns this agreement that would encompass only the wounded, I've never heard of such a thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear Dr. Bosanac say to the civilians that they are to go to Velepromet because an evacuation of civilians was supposed to be carried out from there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard her say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that from anyone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard Mr. Sljivancanin say that when he came to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may we move into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to your meeting with the JNA officers who you claim you saw on the 19th of November inside the hospital. But before we go there, there's something else I want to ask you. On the 19th of November, did you see any TV crews, a cameraman, at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You're talking about the arrival of the JNA representatives, and you're talking about the fact that you saw my client, Mr. Sljivancanin, at this time. Can you please describe a little more closely where you saw him, how you saw him, were there any soldiers around him, and if so, how many. That sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At one time in the afternoon a man appeared on the stairs wearing a camouflage uniform, a green one, with a handful of people. I didn't really count them at the time. He was tall, dark, good-looking. Everything became quiet as he introduced himself: I am Major Sljivancanin. You will now all be taken to Velepromet, and that's where the separation will take place, as previously agreed. That was all. There were a handful of soldiers with him, but I'd be hard-put to say how many exactly. I was in no mind to count or to focus on anything else with the exception of Mr. Sljivancanin himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone react to Mr. Sljivancanin's words to indicate that there was a different interpretation or that a different plan had been agreed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: People just started saying things out loud of their own accord, just like that, spontaneously, but that had no effect on the situation whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember what exactly Mr. Sljivancanin was wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wearing a green camouflage uniform, and the cap was standard issue. We used to refer to it as Tito's cap.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: While you were in the army you probably encountered situations where you familiarised yourself with the different ranks. Did you notice Mr. Sljivancanin's rank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It never even occurred to me to check his rank. He said it himself after all as he introduced himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you expressly remember him introducing himself as "Sljivancanin," the last name of Sljivancanin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: This was on the 19th; more specifically, in the afternoon hours of the 19th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, on the 15th of May, 1992, you gave a statement to the police administration of Vukovar, you gave a statement to an authorised official whose name I will not mention since it is of no relevance to us. You were asked to describe some of the things that had happened in Vukovar. What I want to know is: Were you asked to speak about the arrival of the JNA at the Vukovar Hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not as far as I remember. That wasn't one of the things asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In that statement - I'm not sure if you have a copy in front of you; if not, I'd be glad to provide you with a copy to look at - although you have described to us that you had a verbal conversation with this authorised official, after which a note was compiled. I can read it back for you, if you like, but please just tell me if that reminds you, by any chance, of the conversation between you and this authorised official about what had gone on at the hospital. The note reads: "On the 19th of November, 1991, at about 1800 hours, tall JNA officers arrived within the hospital compound, high-ranking JNA officers arrived in the hospital compound or outside the cellar and started issuing orders for men to go to one side and women and children to the other side." Do you remember saying anything like this to the authorised official talking to you on the 15th of May, 1992, in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I could possibly have said because that just wasn't the way it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I do object again. The procedure is perfectly straightforward and will help all parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you saying the document should be given to the witness at this point?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes. If a witness is going to be cross-examined on a document, he must be given the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Moore, it may be useful for that to happen; it's not a must. Mr. Bulatovic, you do seem to be getting down into detail of what's in the statement, and I think in fairness to the witness, if that's the line that your questioning is to take, he ought to have an opportunity to refresh his recollection of what was in the statement. So if you're pressing on with your question, the witness should see the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I fully understand what you are suggesting; however, I'm afraid the OTP fails to understand. This is precisely what I'm talking about. It's not that the witness said this; I was just reminding him of this conversation he had with an authorised official. That's just what I was asking the witness, whether he remembered saying anything like this. This is a statement signed by this -- if this was a statement signed by this witness, then I would, no doubt, be showing the witness this statement. But he told me that he never said any such thing to the authorised official compiling this statement. I see no point in confronting the witness with this, but that should prove no problem at all if there is enough time. But that is what the objection seems to be about, and I'll ask the witness about other things from that statement, in which case I would like the usher's assistance to please hand the official note to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: As the official note, paragraph 3, reads: "The 19th of November."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Have a look, please. My question: Is this what you spoke about to that authorised official?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already stated, I didn't speak to that authorised official about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What about paragraph 1 of this official note which you have in front of you. It reads: "From the beginning of the aggression of the JNA and the Serb extremists against the city of Vukovar, I was actively involved in the defence as a member of the civil protection until the resistance of the town's defenders was finally broken." Is this something that you spoke to the authorised official about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult now to remember what we talked about verbally. What he wrote down was his own choice.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: This is something you were asked by the OTP yesterday. He mentions some of the names on page 2, suggesting that you spoke to this authorised official about these persons listed in the official note -- or rather, tell me: If you spoke to this authorised official about them, how exactly did you speak to the authorised official about them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just listed the names of people I had noticed at Velepromet and Vupik as well as some details about two or three of them. As for the rest of what this says, it's not something that I stated myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You testified yesterday and there was an objection raised by my learned friend, Borovic, about a particular name. You mentioned some names, but what's added here and what we see next to the names as some activities that those people did --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the last part of counsel's question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All I said was those people were in uniform and armed. As for the rest, I didn't say any of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You probably mentioned these people because they had some distinguishing features. You remembered them because of something that had happened at Velepromet and the hospital, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of these people were people I knew well. Some of them were even my friends or acquaintances.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please explain why back in 1991 you did not mention to this authorised official the JNA officer, Veselin Sljivancanin, as a person who appeared at the hospital, introducing himself, and he seems to play quite an important role there, based on your further testimony.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was this conversation between me and the authorised official, and it's quite natural that omissions should have been made. Maybe he didn't ask, maybe I didn't remember. That's how it was. It was probably an oversight on my part or on his part. To sum it up, Mr. Sljivancanin was not mentioned. I might have said it, but he just failed to record it; that's also possible. What he eventually wrote down was a different thing altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you a while ago and you clearly said that you never discussed this at all. I showed you paragraph 3 of the official note, which speaks about the arrival of JNA officers, and you said you never discussed that at all.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't discuss that at all with this particular authorised official.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In your statement to the OTP you speak about the fact that you saw people from the ECMM and other international organisations, both at Velepromet and at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No; just at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Speaking about the hospital, where exactly did you see the representatives, and what were they doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I emerged from the hospital I was standing on the steps outside and there were two people in white overcoats standing there, talking to Mr. Sljivancanin. They were discussing something -- or rather, I don't know what it was that they were saying, but I clearly heard what Mr. Sljivancanin said to them. They were standing near the steps outside the hospital entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What time was it, can you perhaps remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, unfortunately, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember how long the conversation took?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a very short conversation. I turned around and left. They may as well have gone on with their conversation, but I no longer noticed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You say that you heard Mr. Sljivancanin say something. What did you hear him say to this representative of an international organisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: His voice was raised and he told this person: Go back to your own country if you want to order people about. I'm the one in charge here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you at any time before or after this see these same representatives of the international ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw them again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: My apologies. Did you perhaps see any TV crews anywhere around filming?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You say you didn't see the representatives of international organisations at Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the usher's assistance, please. I would like to show the witness his own statement which he gave on the 19th of June, 1995. Can the witness please have a look. Just in order to save time, this is page 5 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Have you got that, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Where it says: "I saw people from the ICRC"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you read out that sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I saw people from the ICRC at the hospital and at Velepromet." That is indeed what it says, but the fact is I did not see those people at Velepromet.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you arrived at Velepromet you say you did not see any JNA people there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any. Not at Velepromet, at Vupik.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: My understanding is Vupik is just across the way. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement you suggest that you assume that the JNA soldiers were in the centre of town at that time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was an assumption on my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, can you please explain what these mean to you: A member of the JNA, a reservist, a TO member, and eventually a paramilitary belonging to none of the aforementioned categories.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: That's no trouble at all. You held a number of posts which I imagine would enable you to make these important distinctions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the regular JNA, the former JNA, were professional officers and conscripts serving their military term at the time. That is what I would describe as the regular JNA forces, or the former JNA, if you like. All the others were, in my opinion, paramilitaries, persons who joined different kinds of military units and organisations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Along these same lines, did Croatia at the time have a regular army of its own that would meet the criteria that you seem to be espousing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure if you know this. You may have been asked before, in which case I have to apologise: What about members of the so-called HOS; were they involved in the fighting in and around Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've been asked that before, and I clearly stated I didn't see them anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: My apologies in that case. In your statement and in the official note you mentioned quite a number of names. There's one name that I'm particularly interested in. My learned friend Mr. Domazet asked you about this person. I'm talking about Mr. Zigic. You said something about him, what he was, what he did, who he was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What I want to know is: Did you ever see him wear a military uniform before 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. He was a senior inspector with the MUP; that's all he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can we then draw a joint conclusion that we both agree on, that he was no regular member of the JNA. He must have been a member of some TO or paramilitary unit then.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe that he was a regular JNA member.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: After Velepromet, did you ever see this man by the name of Zigic again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at Mitrovica where we were in prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me how long you stayed there. At Mitrovica, I mean.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four months.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Were you subsequently exchanged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prior to that I was in Stajicevo, another camp, for one and a half months, and then I was exchanged in May.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So first you went to Stajicevo and then from Stajicevo you went to Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I'll ask you about this name: Marko Crevar. Does that mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Marko Crevar, that definitely rings a bell. I can't remember right now specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps remember that you saw another person with Zigic at Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the only person I saw nearby was Dr. Maric, but I did not notice anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In answer to one of the questions by my learned friend from the OTP you said that you also knew Stanislav Avramovic, aka Micko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What do you know about him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was just a regular guy, but he was a great football player. He worked at Vuteks with my wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: This man by the name of Avramovic, aka Micko, was he in touch with Martin Dosen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were close friends, at least as far as I know, but that was before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Just in order to -- my apologies -- what I said before -- let me just refresh your memory, perhaps, by telling you, this person I asked you about, Marko Crevar, did he work for the Vukovar SUP? Does that mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that or if Marko Crevar worked for the Vukovar SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of Tomo Gipser, Tomo the plaster technician?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, he applied a cast to my leg, so yes, I do know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what became of him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that he had disappeared.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Where did he disappear from; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where from, but rumour has it that he disappeared.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In the statement you gave to that authorised official, the note which you have in front of you, you mentioned a person by the name of Radivoje Jakovljevic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You say he came to visit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Radivoje Jakovljevic, does he bear any relation to Tomo Gipser?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they are father and son.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you talk to this Radivoje Jakovljevic or did you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just saw him. I think he took a young man away from Stajicevo. I don't know where to, but I later found out that the young man now lives in Australia; in other words, he's still alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Are you familiar with the existence of a shelter at Borovo Komerc?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everyone knows about that one, don't they.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who was in charge of that shelter, or in command, whatever you want to call it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never there throughout the war in Vukovar, and I have no idea who was in charge of that shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything to indicate that Vesna Bosanac's husband was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I did say a while ago that I heard nothing about him throughout.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, while using that sketch, you traced your route from Vupik to Velepromet, if I am not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You say the sketch was made for you by a friend. What I want to know is: Why was this sketch made to begin with? For what purpose?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked to have this made because I wanted to get an idea of where this all occurred. We have some sort of a memorial service annually at Velepromet, so it was a spontaneous request on my part. I asked him to do this for me so that I could look at it and remember more clearly where the buildings and the hangars were, the layout of the Vupik compound, so that one day I am able to share this with my grandchildren and o tell them: This is where your granddad was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And you shared this with the OTP as well, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any photographs to share, by any chance? Photographs in relation to this area in which you were kept.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still have three photographs at home, photographs of Velepromet.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Provided by who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a long time ago. I no longer remember who supplied them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Let us now go back to Velepromet and everything that you have described. I'm talking about your arrival at Velepromet from Vupik. You were brought to a spot which you marked with a letter C on that sketch. Do you remember that, with Boro Rizvanovic who brought you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was outside the carpenter's room, which was later renamed the death room.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Now, if you keep all these different things in mind - Vupik, the hospital, staying there for a while, the bus ride - how long did the whole thing take, how many hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It took quite a while, the entire afternoon and evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So the evening was followed by night. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Was there any public illumination in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When asked by my learned friend Ms. Tapuskovic you testified that you saw Capalo passing by and you said you were 99 per cent --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You testified in a trial taking place before the district court in Belgrade by videolink on the 24th of May, 2005. You were asked by the president of the chamber in charge of the trial about various persons -- about various persons you saw on that day. Some of them you've mentioned here. He asked you specifically about Milan Vojinovic [phoen], aka Capalo. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to put an audio transcript from the trial before the war crimes chamber on the 24th of May, 2005, to put before the witness. In B/C/S, that's page 10/21. My apologies. I don't know whether the OTP has managed to locate the portion I intend to quote, since I don't have the English version with me. I would kindly ask the witness to read aloud slowly from page 10 towards the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: It states there: "Witness -" and I will not mention your name, and the last sentence. Could you read it aloud.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last line: "I saw Capalo at Velepromet."

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Does this refresh your memory about mentioning Capalo when you testified before the war crimes chamber in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just replied to their questions, as recorded here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this concludes my cross-examination. I would like to thank the witness, and I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Bulatovic. Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Witness, would you be kind enough to go to the transcript that's just been cited to you by the Defence. In the English version it is page 14 of 28 for the translation that I have, and my B/C/S is not quite up to speed, so I can't tell the page for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Is that the same page that my learned friend is referring to? Because I do have: "I saw Capalo at Velepromet." Can I just clarify if the witness now has got a B/C/S version of that question. I notice my learned friend is saying "yes."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: You're asked -- have you got that, Witness, that particular reference to the question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: The first question that I have got, and just above that, is president of the committee. "A. No, there is also Capalo, but he died." Do you have that part?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And then the next question, I think it's a question my learned friend referred to in cross-examination. You say: "I saw Capalo in Velepromet." Is that the same place that's being referred to? Is that right, Witness, or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And then the next question is from the president of the committee: "Do you know any other Vojinovic, Milan?" Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Were you ever asked by anyone what you saw Capalo doing or carrying that evening? Just look at that, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never, no one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we just put that away, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Would Your Honour forgive me a moment while I just locate some papers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can I just clarify from my learned friends, in relation to the allegation by the Prosecution that Sljivancanin was telling people that they were to be taken to Velepromet and to be separated there, is that accepted by my learned friend that that occurred? Because if it isn't accepted, I will deal with it in re-examination. That was never put in direct terms, whether they agreed or did not agree that that was the case. Could they assist me on that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you. The very fact that there were -- questions were asked of the witness by the Defence I believe makes it clear that we cannot accept that, and our questions were put precisely in that direction, to deny that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. That's made the position clear. Yes, Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So you understand, what is being suggested to you, Witness, by the Defence, what they're saying is that you didn't see Sljivancanin outside the hospital on the evening of the 19th, and that he didn't tell people to be -- to go to Velepromet and be separated. Now, what do you say to that suggestion? Do you agree with that or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe my learned friend of the OTP misinterpreted the words of the Defence. We never disputed Mr. Sljivancanin's presence on the 19th in the afternoon in front of the hospital; therefore, it cannot be seen as such. And as regards the other fact, I just stated my opinion as to what, in our estimate, Mr. Sljivancanin was doing and who was with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: In my submission, the witness is entitled to know whether, in actual fact, the Defence are saying that Sljivancanin said to witnesses -- or said to people there that they were to go to Velepromet, and that's where the separation occurred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: As I understood it, that is not accepted by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: His presence at the hospital is accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I can clarify it then this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Witness, are you aware that the Defence do not accept that you heard Sljivancanin telling people they were going to go to Velepromet and be separated? Now, what do you say to that? Did you hear Sljivancanin say that or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I claim full responsibility that he did and said what I stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Was there any importance to you and other people there that such a statement was made?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was very important.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Why was it important --

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe this will be a textbook example of a leading question, because it comprises an element of reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, I submit, we're reading different textbooks. I would submit that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Your question is in order, Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Why was it important to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we were hoping to leave the hospital for the direction desired, as we were informed. But according to what Mr. Sljivancanin had to say, there was another plan or another order, and we were deeply struck by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: You were asked about the report that was compiled on the 15th of May, 1992. Now, do you have that document -- document before you? And if not, perhaps could you be shown the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, I'm told there's no hard copy, but there is an e-court edition, and the number is 03577927. Your Honour, I'm told actually we have now found a hard copy in B/C/S, and often people find that easier. May I pass that to the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, what I would like you to do, please, is here we have got a report and you have told us about the way you believe it was compiled. I don't want to go into that again. And what's being suggested to you is -- well, why no mention of Mr. Sljivancanin's name. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can we just look through this document slowly, because your evidence in cross-examination was -- well, you were asked various questions and you gave names in reply. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can we just go through the document, then, please. Now, I cannot correlate the various paragraphs and pages because they're not numbered, but if I do it in a general way, is it right that in actual fact in this document there are something approaching 38 names given by you of people you recognised? Just have a look at it, please. Take your time and just check.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And the names that you gave, were they people that you knew personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And what was the purpose of giving these names in this particular report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asked that by the interviewer. The question was: Who was it that I saw in the hospital at Velepromet and at Vupik, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: But the question was: Were these people that you knew personally? You knew their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further re-examination, but I would make application that this particular report, which was compiled on the 15th of May, 1992, be made an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: On what basis, Mr. Moore?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: On the basis that there has been cross-examination that the omission of the name of Sljivancanin is a factor that the Court should take into account indicating, I suspect, that the name "Sljivancanin" only arose in the 1995 document and presumably was a subsequent creation. In my submission, the purpose of putting this document before the Court is the Court would be able to assess by its content and context and the structure of the document what the purpose was in respect of its compilation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So you do not propose it be received as proof of its content?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But for the purpose of assessing the credibility witness in relation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit 190 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Moore. Sir, you will be pleased to know that that concludes the questions of you, so that in a few moments when we rise you will be able to leave the court and return to your home. The Chamber would thank you for coming to The Hague and for the assistance that you've given us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're in a position to resume with another witness, are we, Mr. Moore, after the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. The next witness is a protected witness, and Mr. Smith will be dealing with that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn now and resume at --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- 20 minutes to the hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
